newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares weaken, led by property.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares weaken, led by property.

text.p: Singapore shares shrugged off Wall Street's gains and fell by midday on Tuesday, led by property counters on concerns over the domestic supply surplus.

Dealers said the sector was dampened by the announcement of plans by the Port of Singapore Authority (PSA) and Keppel Corp to turn harbour sites into residential projects. That renewed focus on Sembawang's yard redevelopment plan.
Property heavyweights City Development Ltd and DBS Land hit new year lows after shedding Singapore $1.10 and S$0.06 respectively to S$10.30 and S$4.30.
At 0430 GMT, CityDev was at S$10.80, down S$0.60 while DBS Land was at S$4.32, down four cents.
The two counters pushed the SES property index down 14.66 points, or 2.33 percent, to 614.47.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was down 13.74 points at 1,905.11, dragged by property-linked Cycle & Carriage and the local tranche of Singapore Press Holding.
Small-capitalised stocks like hotel group Amara Holdings were traded actively. Amara was flat at S$0.425, with over 6.3 million shares.
Keppel Corp retreated as the initial euphoria over its site redevelopment plans faded. After hitting a morning high of S$6.35, it fell to S$6.05, down S$0.15 with over 3.5 million shares traded.

"The news was positively received. But on analysis, the appeal of the joint development diminished because what's been confirmed so far has been a joint development for the common boundary of eight to nine hectares it shares with PSA," said an investment analyst with a local house.
Sembawang Corp firmed 15 cents to S$6.65 on expectations that its interim profits, expected to be announced later this week, would be higher than forecast.
